title: After an attack on a family, Guneku turns to its Palace — and the case goes to the gendarmerie
excerpt: Following a reported attack on a family in Guneku, the community turned to the Palace. Suspects were questioned there on 2 October 2026 and the case was passed to the gendarmerie. Fondom Studios documented the proceedings.
sourceNote: Written fresh on 17 October 2026 from two public community sources — the Fondom Studios documentary (published 5 October 2026, 21:20 UTC) and the Mbengwi Info Newsline post of 2 October 2026 — and from the community intelligence review of the same date, which sampled the documentary's footage and read the village community group. A report that the suspects came from a neighbouring village is unconfirmed and is deliberately not repeated. No photograph is reproduced: the circulating images show the suspects, and the victims are protected. No person is named. Recorded allegations are reported as allegations; no court outcome is established in either source.
body:
This record concerns an alleged attack on children. The victims are not identified here and should not be identified anywhere. The suspects have not been tried.

What was reported

A family home in Guneku was attacked. According to the account published by Fondom Studios, two young girls were allegedly attacked inside their home, and about 120,000 FCFA was reportedly taken from the family. The allegations reported in the community include robbery and sexual assault.

The community and the Palace

Rather than leave the matter to rumour, the community turned to the Guneku Palace and its traditional institutions. A quiet investigation followed: information was gathered and suspects were identified.

On Friday 2 October 2026, the suspects were brought before the Palace for questioning. According to the documentary, items were recovered in the course of the investigation, and the case was then passed to the gendarmerie. Mbengwi Info Newsline reported the same afternoon that the security forces had taken the suspects to Mbengwi for further questioning, and that the village was calm. The documentary's closing footage shows the suspects being collected by the gendarmerie.

Community leaders in Guneku called for vigilance, and urged people not to take the law into their own hands but to report suspicious movements to the proper authorities.

What is confirmed, and what is only reported

  • Confirmed by more than one source: that suspects were questioned at the Palace on 2 October 2026, and that they were then handed to the gendarmerie and taken to Mbengwi.
  • Reported by a single source: that about 120,000 FCFA was taken, and that items were recovered. What the items were is not stated.
  • An allegation, with no court finding: the sexual assault of the two girls.
  • Not known: the date of the attack itself, beyond its being before 2 October, and any charge, trial or outcome.

Where the matter stands

The suspects are subject to the ordinary legal process. Statements or admissions reported during the questioning at the Palace are not a court judgment, and nobody is guilty of anything until a court says so. No charge, trial or verdict has been reported in the sources reviewed up to 17 October 2026. This record will be updated if one is.

In the days that followed, the men of Fun Quarter performed traditional rites to protect the land, in response to the insecurity — see Fun Quarter performs traditional rites to protect the land.

Sources

  • Fondom Studios — documentary published on 5 October 2026, Guneku ritual vs thieves & rapist suspects: traditional investigation, Guneku Palace, 2 October 2026. Watch the documentary on Facebook. Fondom Studios states that the victims' identities and private details have been protected, and asks viewers not to try to identify them.
  • Mbengwi Info Newsline — post of 2 October 2026. Read the post on Facebook.
